questions.q: Who is the Catalan architect known for his highly individualistic, organic style, including the Sagrada Família?
questions.n: He is the definitive figure of Catalan Modernism whose works are characterized by unique organic forms inspired by nature.

questions.q: Which Spanish architect is the primary figure of Catalan Modernism?
questions.n: Gaudí is globally recognized as the leading figure and most influential representative of the Modernisme movement.

questions.q: Who designed the glass and steel Pyramid that serves as the main entrance to the Louvre Museum in Paris?
questions.n: Pei's modernist design for the Louvre was controversial at first but has since become a global landmark.

questions.q: The Louvre Pyramid in France is a renowned work by which Chinese-American architect?
questions.n: Pei's Pritzker-winning career is defined by clean lines and the use of geometric forms like the pyramid.

questions.q: Which Filipino architect is recognized for his versatility and mastery of the Art Nouveau and Beaux-Arts styles?
questions.n: Antonio is celebrated for his pioneering role in Filipino Modernism and his skill in Art Deco and related styles.

questions.q: Who is the German architect famous for the expressionist design of the Einstein Tower in Potsdam?
questions.n: Mendelsohn used dynamic, sculptural forms in the Einstein Tower, making it a masterpiece of architectural expressionism.

questions.q: Which architect designed the historic Manila Hotel in the Philippines?
questions.n: Parsons was the consulting architect for the Philippine Commission who designed the landmark hotel.

questions.q: Which British architect is known for the high-tech design of the Reichstag restoration and the Gherkin?
questions.n: Lord Foster is the head of Foster + Partners, the firm responsible for these iconic structural feats.

questions.q: Who is the Brazilian architect famous for designing the civic buildings of Brasília?
questions.n: Niemeyer is renowned for his sculptural use of reinforced concrete in buildings like the Cathedral of Brasília.

questions.q: Which American architect is known for his geometric, white Neomodernist designs like the Getty Center?
questions.n: Meier is famous for his strict adherence to white surfaces and rationalist geometric grids.

questions.q: What is the branch of architecture and engineering that deals with the design and organization of urban space and activities?
questions.n: This discipline manages the land use, infrastructure, and social aspects of urban environments.

questions.q: Which design philosophy focuses on building in harmony with the hot-humid climate of regions like the Philippines?
questions.n: Tropical design prioritizes natural ventilation and shading to deal with high temperatures and humidity.

questions.q: What is the term for design that meets current needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet theirs?
questions.n: This definition comes from the Brundtland Report, emphasizing long-term resource preservation.

questions.q: What cooling method relies on natural energy (wind and sun) rather than mechanical systems?
questions.n: Passive systems use architectural features to manage heat and airflow without electricity.

questions.q: What is the effect where wind speed increases when passing through a narrow opening between buildings?
questions.n: In urban design, this explains why wind feels stronger in narrow alleys or between skyscrapers.

questions.q: Which strategy involves placing windows on opposite sides of a room to facilitate airflow?
questions.n: Placing openings on opposite sides creates a pressure difference that pulls air through the space.

questions.q: What do you call the vertical shaft used in passive cooling to allow hot air to escape through the roof?
questions.n: Hot air rises and creates a vacuum that draws cooler air in from lower levels.

questions.q: In tropical design, what is the purpose of wide roof eaves?
o: To provide shade and protect walls from heavy rainfall
To serve as a structural support for gutters
questions.n: In the Philippines, wide eaves keep the sun off walls and prevent rain from entering open windows.

questions.q: What is the term for the total solar radiation energy received on a given surface area?
questions.n: Short for 'Incoming Solar Radiation,' it is a key factor in calculating heat gain.

questions.q: Which orientation is generally avoided for large glass windows in the Philippines to minimize heat gain?
questions.n: The low morning and afternoon sun hits these walls directly, making them hardest to cool.

questions.q: What does the acronym CPD stand for in the context of professional regulation?
questions.n: CPD refers to the ongoing learning requirements for professionals to maintain their license.

questions.q: Under the PRC, what refers to the inculcation of advanced knowledge, skills, and ethical values in a post-licensure specialized or interdisciplinary field?
questions.n: This is the formal definition used in Philippine professional law to ensure competence.

questions.q: What is the standard minimum headroom clearance for a means of egress?
questions.n: This is the standard minimum required by building codes to prevent injury during exit.

questions.q: What is the standard recommended width for a shower door?
questions.n: 0.60m is the standard functional width for shower entries.

questions.q: What is the standard minimum width for a bedroom door?
questions.n: 0.80m is the accepted minimum to allow for furniture passage and occupant comfort.

questions.q: What is the standard minimum width for a main entry door?
questions.n: Main entry doors are wider to accommodate larger items and provide a clear primary path.

questions.q: Which SPP document covers Pre-Design Services?
questions.n: Document 201 covers initial feasibility, programming, and site selection services.

questions.q: Which SPP document covers Regular Design Services?
questions.n: 202 defines the six phases of the architect's regular design work.

questions.q: Which SPP document covers Specialized Allied Services?
questions.n: Document 203 includes interior design, landscape, acoustics, and other specialties.

questions.q: Which SPP document covers Full-Time Supervision Services?
questions.n: This specific sub-document deals with the architect's role in daily site supervision.

questions.q: Which SPP document covers Construction Management Services?
questions.n: 204-B outlines the duties and responsibilities of the Construction Manager.

questions.q: Which SPP document covers Post-Construction Services?
questions.n: 205 covers maintenance, building administration, and post-occupancy evaluation.

questions.q: Under SPP 203, what is the recommended minimum fee for interior design or furniture detailing?
o: 6% to 10% of the cost of the work
20% to 25% of the cost of the work
5% to 8% of the cost of the work
10% to 15% of the cost of the work (10% as base minimum)
questions.n: This is the standard recommended percentage for these highly specialized design services.

questions.q: If an architect is asked to design a pool, cabinetry, and movable furniture, under which SPP document does this fall?
questions.n: These fall under specialized categories such as landscape design and interior design.

questions.q: What is the minimum basic fee for a specialized service like acoustic design under SPP 203?
o: 10% to 15% of the cost of the work
questions.n: Like interior design, acoustics is a specialized service requiring this higher fee range.

questions.q: What is the primary law regulating the practice of architecture in the Philippines?
questions.n: RA 9266 is the current, active law that governs the profession.

questions.q: What is the official title of RA 9266?
o: The United Architects of the Philippines Charter
The National Building and Architecture Act
questions.n: This is the formal name given to Republic Act No. 9266.

questions.q: Who has the power to revoke or suspend a Certificate of Registration of an architect?
o: The United Architects of the Philippines (UAP)
The Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH)
The Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture (PRBOA)
questions.n: The PRBOA handles the administrative and quasi-judicial functions related to architectural practice.

questions.q: What is the validity period of an Architect’s Professional Identification Card?
questions.n: Renewal is required every three years on the architect's birth month.

questions.q: Who is the only person legally allowed to sign and seal architectural plans?
questions.n: Registration and licensing are mandatory requirements to legally sign and seal documents.

questions.q: Under PD 957, what is the minimum lot area for an Open Market Single Detached unit?
questions.n: Open Market Single Detached lots require more space than Medium Cost lots.

questions.q: Under PD 957, what is the minimum lot area for a Medium Cost Single Detached unit?
questions.n: Medium Cost units have a slightly smaller minimum requirement than Open Market ones.

questions.q: Under PD 957, what is the minimum lot area for an Open Market Duplex/Semi-Detached unit?
questions.n: Open Market Duplex units require 96sqm per unit.

questions.q: Under PD 957, what is the minimum lot area for a Medium Cost Duplex/Semi-Detached unit?
questions.n: Medium Cost Duplex units must meet this 80sqm minimum.

questions.q: Under BP 220, what is the minimum lot area for an Economic Single Detached unit?
questions.n: Economic housing requires slightly larger lots than Socialized housing.

questions.q: Under BP 220, what is the minimum lot area for a Socialized Single Detached unit?
questions.n: Socialized housing allows for a minimum of 64sqm for single detached homes.

questions.q: Under BP 220, what is the minimum lot area for an Economic Duplex/Semi-Detached unit?
questions.n: BP 220 Economic Duplex units have a 54sqm minimum.

questions.q: Under BP 220, what is the minimum lot area for a Socialized Duplex/Semi-Detached unit?
questions.n: The minimum requirement for a socialized duplex is 48sqm per unit.

questions.q: Under BP 220, what is the minimum lot area for an Economic Rowhouse?
questions.n: Economic rowhouses are smaller than duplexes, with a 36sqm minimum.

questions.q: Under BP 220, what is the minimum lot area for a Socialized Rowhouse?
questions.n: 28sqm is the smallest allowed lot area for any housing type under these regulations.
